messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: /alerts/inference-5xx-rate spike in az=az1b region=eu-central1. 5xx rate >= 4% for 5m, p95 latency up 2x. Triggered paging to oncall-infra

oncall-infra: oncall here, acked. I see increased resolver RTTs and intermittent ENI TX errors from a subset of instances. beginning triage now.

sre-zoe: joining. can you paste the top failing ASGs and recent kernel log snippets?

oncall-infra: top hit is inference-pool-eu-az1b (g5.xlarge equivalents). Netstat shows retransmits. grabbing dmesg and netstat output:

```
# recent dmesg tail
[ 12345.678] ixgbe 0000:af:00.1: device reset
[ 12346.001] net_eth0: tx timeout, resetting
```

```
# netstat -s | grep retrans
TCP retransmited segments: 4321
```

eng-runtime: sounds like host NIC flaps causing packet loss. Are health checks failing at the LB?

oncall-infra: yes, NLB target health shows 20% unhealthy, but unhealthy targets are spread — looks like soft-reset causing connections to stall, not full instance death. DNS resolvers for the AZ also show spike in response latency (50-300ms).

support-lead: any customer impact numbers? need to know who to notify and scope.

oncall-infra: preliminary: ~3.8% request-level 5xx across eu-central1 for last 10m. p95 generation latency up from 120ms to 520ms for affected AZ. Top affected customers: 7 accounts with high concurrency, two with realtime inference SLAs.

eng-runtime: propose immediate mitigations: 1) shift 60% of inference traffic away from az1b to eu-central1a/1c via routing policy, 2) lower DNS TTL to 5s for our service domain to accelerate resolver refresh, 3) scale up spare capacity in eu-central1a. I can run the routing canary if ops approves.

ops-liz: I can kick traffic-redispatch now. command:

```
traffic-redispatch --from az1b --to eu-central1a,eu-central1c --percent 60 --canary 10
```

ops-liz: kicked canary 10% to eu-central1a/c. watching metrics.

incident-bot: action logged: traffic-redispatch started by ops-liz (run id: tr-2026-177123).

oncall-infra: after canary, error rate on default pool dropped from 3.8% to 1.1% for requests routed away. p95 for shifted traffic ~140ms. still seeing ~2.5% 5xx stuck on remaining az1b capacity.

sre-zoe: lower TTL change request submitted to DNS team (ticket #DNS-421). keep TTL at 5s for 20m and monitor for resolver amplification.

eng-runtime: also rolling a model-variant fallback on affected instances to smaller quantized model to reduce per-request network chatter and keep tail latency down. triggering via rollout api: `rollout-model inference-base -> inference-base-quant -% 100 --scope az1b`

support-lead: prepping customer comms: saying degraded performance in eu-central1 due to AZ network instability, mitigations in progress (traffic shift + scaling). ETA unknown, will update in 30m.

oncall-infra: ops: can we cordon suspect hosts to avoid oscillation? I can `kubectl drain` but that will cause immediate pod reschedules. Suggest draining lowest-util hosts first.

ops-liz: doing staggered drain of 3 nodes in inference-pool-eu-az1b: `kubectl drain node-a node-b node-c --ignore-daemonsets --grace-period=30`

incident-bot: event: node-c cordoned by ops-liz.

oncall-infra: after draining three hosts, NLB unhealthy count reduced to 8%, 5xx rate down to 1.2% cluster-wide. p95 approaching normal for shifted traffic.

sre-zoe: recommendation: keep traffic shift at 60% for now, complete cordon/drain of remaining suspect hosts, follow-up with cloud provider ticket for ENI flaps. I'll own postmortem.

eng-runtime: agree. I'll keep the model fallback active in az1b until node health stable. Also adding a temporary routing policy to prefer eu-central1a for new sessions.

support-lead: sent initial high-touch note to two SLA customers, added incident status page update.

oncall-infra: handing off to eng-runtime and sre-zoe for longer-term fix and postmortem. oncall clear for now, keep channel for updates. :thumbsup:

ops-liz: leaving watch on metrics for 30m, will escalate to cloud provider if flaps continue.

sre-zoe: copying runbooks and will open incident postmortem. tagging with root-cause hypothesis: az1b NIC firmware interaction with host kernel under high TX load.

support-lead: noted. prepping a follow-up comms with timeline once we have cloud provider acknowledgment.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> partial: error rate reduced from 3.8% to 1.0%. handover complete.

eng-runtime: thanks everyone. handing channel to postmortem owners.
